what: Plan wires the new lint only through Makefile, not the actual pre-commit hook suite
scenario_or_breakage: `pre-commit run --all-files`, the installed git hook, and `scripts/relevant-checks.sh` all use `.pre-commit-config.yaml`; adding only Makefile targets leaves the claimed pre-commit lint unenforced on those paths
suggested_fix: Add a local `.pre-commit-config.yaml` hook for `scripts/lint-readability-preamble.sh`; put `test-lint-readability-preamble` in one `test-harnesses-N` shard instead of only adding both targets directly to `lint`

what: The lint manifest and grep contract do not explicitly exclude non-amendment files, including `readability-style.md` itself
scenario_or_breakage: `readability-style.md` must declare `<READABILITY_STYLE>` and may contain examples, so including it in the hard-coded manifest would always satisfy the token check without proving any prompt references the preamble; the same false-pass risk applies to lint docs or tests that mention the token/directive prose
suggested_fix: Spell out the manifest as only real amendment sites and exclude `skills/design/references/readability-style.md`, `scripts/lint-readability-preamble.sh`, `scripts/lint-readability-preamble.md`, and the test harness; make each manifest row declare the expected variant

what: The two grep patterns are too broad for the enforcement they claim
scenario_or_breakage: Plain `<READABILITY_STYLE>` and `MANDATORY .* readability-style\.md` can pass on contract prose, examples, comments, or documentation text while the actual prompt body or orchestrator instruction omits the style requirement
suggested_fix: Use exact anchored checks for the intended line forms, such as `^Style requirements: \`<READABILITY_STYLE>\`\.$` for external prompt bodies and a line-start `**MANDATORY — READ ENTIRE FILE before ...: \`skills/design/references/readability-style.md\`.` pattern for inline directives

what: The lint harness only specifies one non-compliant fixture, not one per accepted pattern variant
scenario_or_breakage: A bug in the MANDATORY-directive branch could ship if the lone failing fixture only removes the substitution token, or vice versa
suggested_fix: Split negative coverage into at least two isolated cases: one external-prompt fixture missing the token and one orchestrator-inline fixture missing the MANDATORY readability directive; assert the offending path for each

what: Plan-review prompt changes target the reference doc but omit the renderer that actually emits reviewer prompts
scenario_or_breakage: Updating `skills/design/references/plan-review.md` alone will not add the readability preamble to static plan-review prompts because `render-plan-review-prompt.sh` hard-codes the emitted prompt body
suggested_fix: Add `skills/design/scripts/render-plan-review-prompt.sh` and `skills/design/scripts/test-plan-review-prompt.sh` to the plan, read/insert the preamble there, and assert the rendered prompt contains the style guidance

what: The brainstorm-synthesis directive is assigned to `SKILL.md`, but the synthesis-writing instructions live in `brainstorm.md`
scenario_or_breakage: An implementer can add the directive near the Step 1d.5 entry point while the actual `brainstorm.md` synthesis section remains unchanged, so the writer of `$DESIGN_TMPDIR/brainstorm.md` may never be told to read the preamble
suggested_fix: Move that planned directive to `skills/design/references/brainstorm.md` immediately before `## Synthesis → brainstorm.md`, and include that file in the lint manifest as a MANDATORY-directive site

what: The sketch plan includes `GENERIC_PROMPT`, but the current sketch prompt file has only four prompt bodies and SIMPLE mode launches no sketch prompt
scenario_or_breakage: Adding or linting a generic prompt would be scope creep for this change and may create an unused amendment site
suggested_fix: Drop `GENERIC_PROMPT` from the planned sketch-prompts change unless the PR also intentionally changes SIMPLE sketch behavior, which would exceed the minimum-change lane
